sections.title: Premise
sections.why: The premise is the shortest true statement of your story, and every other entry in the bible has to agree with it.

seed.label: Seed
seed.guide: One sentence, under 15 words, with no character names.
questions: Who has the most to lose? Describe them without using a name.
What do they want to win, or keep from losing?
What larger situation puts that at risk?
Put those together in one sentence of fewer than 15 words.

sketch.label: Sketch
sketch.guide: One paragraph of about five sentences: the setup, three disasters, and the ending.
questions: Setup: who, where, and what’s normal before things go wrong?
First disaster: what ends the beginning and commits them? It can come from outside.
Second disaster: how does their attempt to fix things make it worse?
Third disaster: what failure forces the final act?
Ending: how does it resolve, and what does it cost?

sheet.label: Sheet
sheet.guide: About a page, in four paragraphs. Each of the first three ends in a disaster.
questions: Who, where, and what’s normal, up to the first disaster that commits them?
How does their first attempt to fix things lead to the second disaster?
What do they try next, and what failure forces the final act?
How does it resolve, and what does it cost them?
